key_evidence_accepted: There was consistent evidence on record to prove harassment for dowry soon before the death of the deceased. The deceased died within 10 months of the marriage. According to PW3, father of the deceased, after three months of the marriage, the deceased informed him that the appellant and his family were harassing her for dowry. He, along with PW-12, went to the house of the appellant and requested them not to harass her. Again, three days before the occurrence, on 28th April, 2001, the deceased informed her father about the dowry harassment on which her uncle PW-12, along with his wife, went to the house of the accused and brought the deceased to her parental home. The appellant took her away on the threat of divorce and on the next day, she died of burn injuries.
witness_credibility: The court assessed the main witnesses as credible, noting that Kashmiri Lal, Guddar Mal, and Raghubir Lal have specifically and categorically deposed about the demand of dowry soon before her death. The suicide note was not considered as an encyclopedia of the entire situation and was not sufficient to exonerate the appellant.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 2001; Trial judgment: 12.03.2013; High Court decision: 12.03.2013; Supreme Court decision: November 14, 2014
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: G.C. Shahpuri; Counsel for the State: Kamal Mohan Gupta
investigation_status: First Information Report (FIR) lodged; charge sheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction upheld; High Court: Conviction upheld; Supreme Court: Appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that there was consistent evidence to prove harassment for dowry by the husband soon before the death of the victim-deceased, and that the husband's actions led to the deceased's suicide by burn injuries.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the prosecution failed to prove the demand of dowry 'soon before the death' and that the deceased's suicide note indicated she was not being harassed. They also claimed the appellant's case should be treated at par with his mother and brother who were acquitted.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that harassment for dowry 'soon before the death' is a necessary ingredient for the offence under Section 304-B of the IPC, and that the statutory presumption under Section 113B of the Evidence Act applies when such harassment is proven.
precedent_relied_upon: Hira Lal and Ors. vs. State (Govt. of NCT) Delhi 2003 (1) Suppl. SCR 734; Manohar Lal vs. State of Haryana AIR (2014) SC 2555
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because there was consistent evidence of harassment for dowry soon before the death of the deceased, and the husband's responsibility towards his wife was deemed higher than that of other relatives.
other_sentence_order: The appellant is directed to surrender to undergo the remaining sentence, failing which he may be arrested and committed to custody to complete the sentence awarded to him.
